summary: 58-year-old African-Caribbean man, no urinary symptoms, asks about "the prostate test". USPSTF 2018: at 55–69 an individual decision after discussing benefits and harms; Black men may particularly benefit from the discussion.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Asking about the prostate blood test
inputs.hpi: Asymptomatic 58-year-old man of African-Caribbean descent. Two friends have had prostate cancer and he asks whether he should have a PSA test. No urinary frequency, nocturia once, good stream. No bone pain. No family history of prostate cancer.
inputs.socialHistory: Taxi owner. Ex-smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 20 years ago.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Prostate cancer screening discussion — age 58
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic 58-year-old African-Caribbean man. Shared decision on PSA screening: benefits (small reduction in prostate cancer death) and harms (false positives, biopsy, overdiagnosis, treatment effects) discussed.

mustInclude.note: Grade C: an individual decision after discussion, not an automatic test.

mustExclude.note: No PSA result yet: no biopsy or MRI.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Over-triage: 'Two friends have had prostate cancer' → 'Possible malignancy' (priority) → same_day_call.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Treat topic words ('cancer screening', a relative's cancer) as context rather than a current malignancy red flag, and treat 'no change in bowel habit' as negated (the matcher currently handles 'no change' as a pseudo-negation).

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for prostate cancer
guideline.section: 55–69: individual decision about PSA-based screening after discussion of potential benefits and harms (grade C); ≥ 70: recommend against PSA-based screening (grade D); Black men and men with a family history may benefit from the discussion
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for prostate cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2018;319:1901–1913.

rationale: PSA screening at 55–69 is a preference-sensitive decision. The output should support an informed discussion rather than an automatic test, and certainly not a diagnostic pathway.

authoring.author: Claude (prevention/screening, obstetric-gynaecological mimics and paediatric surgery cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Every citation is verified: false. iOS outcomes are unverified (not run on Linux); triage after the first CI run.
